def: A non-profit web crawl published as periodic snapshots of billions of pages, the main raw source of text for pretraining.
Pulling the main prose out of a web page's HTML while discarding navigation, adverts and other boilerplate.
An experiment that removes or changes one step of a pipeline and measures the effect, usually by training a small model with and without it.
Removing repeated documents, lines or passages from a training corpus so the model does not waste compute on, or memorise, repeated text.
The size of the overlap of two sets divided by the size of their union, used to measure how alike two documents' shingle sets are.
An overlapping run of n consecutive words (or characters) taken from a document so it can be treated as a set for similarity comparison.
A way to compress a set into a short signature so that the chance two signature values match equals the sets' Jaccard similarity.
Splitting signatures into bands and bucketing by band so that only likely near-duplicates are ever compared with each other.
A small model trained to score how closely a document resembles a reference set of good text, used to keep the highest-scoring pages.
The fraction of training tokens drawn from each source, such as web, code, maths and multilingual text.
Choosing each source with probability proportional to its size raised to a power below one, so that small sources are upsampled.
A final stretch of training, as the learning rate falls to zero, in which the mix is shifted towards very high-quality data.
